key_highlights: ASX edged higher on Wall Street strength but Corporate Travel (CTX.AX) plunged, signalling sector-specific weakness
Mortgage stress at 18-year highs and house prices forecast to fall 10% ahead of a potential fourth RBA rate hike
Australia's economy narrowly avoided recession; productivity rated 'bad to worse', undermining Chalmers' 'strong economy' narrative
Treasury yields hit 19-month high as global bond woes spread; AUD under pressure from inflation concerns
Persian Gulf tanker fires and geopolitical tensions (China missile test, Venezuela) elevate energy and risk-premium risks
Labor's 30% discretionary trust tax draft and small-business workaround signal major tax policy shift
Gold exploration activity surges: Dalaroo, PLC, Auric ($28M profit), Gateway (Wiluna discovery), Critical (NZ targets)
Qantas (QAN.AX) faces dual pressure: ground crew strike vote and cost-cutting on island routes

sectors.trend: Gold exploration and production activity accelerating across WA and Africa; rare earths and lithium exploration expanding. Chinese solar overtaking coal supports long-term metals demand but near-term commodity prices under pressure.
sectors.implications: Junior miners (Dalaroo, PLC, Gateway, Critical) see elevated exploration spend; Auric's $28M profit validates WA gold economics. Lindian's 20-yr Kazakhstan rare earths offtake de-risks that segment. BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX face mixed iron ore/coal demand signals.

sectors.trend: Mortgage stress at 18-year highs and potential 10% house price decline threaten NPL trajectories. RBA rate-hike uncertainty creates earnings volatility. Trust tax changes may alter wealth-management revenue streams.
sectors.implications: CBA.AX, NAB.AX, ANZ.AX, WBC.AX face rising credit-cost pressure. REITs (VGP.AX, SGP.AX) vulnerable to rate-driven cap-rate expansion. Trust tax draft (30%) could reduce discretionary trust income flows into banks.

sectors.trend: Persian Gulf tanker fires spike oil risk premium. Tasmania power station fire threatens grid reliability. Energy transition costs 'running off the rails'. One Nation pushing coal plant retention vs. Chinese solar overtaking coal globally.
sectors.implications: SOL.AX, WDS.AX, AWE.AX face policy uncertainty. Gas cartel concerns (Beetaloo) may support AGL.AX, CSG.AX pricing. Grid reliability issues favour infrastructure plays.

sectors.trend: Qantas (QAN.AX) under operational stress: strike vote, cost cuts, luggage price hikes. Corporate Travel (CTX.AX) plunged. Grocery theft rising. Small business sentiment fragile post-Covid.
sectors.implications: QAN.AX faces margin compression and industrial risk. CTX.AX weakness signals softening corporate travel demand. WES.AX, WOW.AX may see modest defensive rotation.

sectors.trend: Nvidia signals AI boom continues; global semiconductor recovery underway (Qorvo/Skyworks merger, Arrow, Vishay). Fabrinet flagged as AI infrastructure play.
sectors.implications: Limited direct ASX exposure but supports global risk appetite. CSL.AX and healthcare tech may benefit from AI-driven diagnostics. ASX tech names remain thin.

key_themes: RBA rate-hike risk vs. recession-avoidance: economy limping, productivity deteriorating, but policymakers cautious
Housing market stress: 18-year high mortgage stress, 10% price decline forecast, developer insolvencies (Bathla, fugitive developer)
Geopolitical risk premium: Persian Gulf tanker fires, China missile test, Venezuela crisis, US-Australia military acceleration
Tax policy overhaul: 30% discretionary trust tax, small-business workarounds, KPMG scandal fallout
Commodity and energy transition tension: coal vs. solar, gas cartel, grid reliability
Global bond stress: 19-month high treasury yields, spreading bond woes

risk_assessment.risk_factor: RBA rate hike triggering housing correction
risk_assessment.mitigation: Reduce REIT and home-loan-heavy bank exposure; favour fixed-income and dividend aristocrats
Maintain energy hedges; monitor BHP.AX, WDS.AX oil exposure; hold gold as safe haven
Favour cost-controlled sectors (healthcare, staples); avoid rate-sensitive growth

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Qantas industrial action and airline sector disruption
risk_assessment.mitigation: Avoid QAN.AX near-term; monitor travel demand via CTX.AX

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Trust tax policy shift disrupting wealth flows
risk_assessment.mitigation: Review discretionary trust structures; monitor financials for AUM impact

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Global bond market stress / rising yields
risk_assessment.mitigation: Shorten duration; favour floating-rate and equity income over long bonds

opportunities.rationale: Geopolitical risk premium, 19-month high yields, and strong WA gold production (Auric $28M profit, Gateway Wiluna discovery) support gold pricing

opportunities.recommendation: Selective energy exposure on grid reliability and gas
opportunities.rationale: Tasmania fire, energy transition cost overruns, and gas cartel concerns support AGL, CSG, and infrastructure plays

opportunities.recommendation: Rare earths and critical minerals positioning
opportunities.rationale: Lindian 20-yr Kazakhstan offtake, ZhongNuo/Chariot Nigerian lithium, True North copper expansion signal structural demand

defensive_moves.rationale: 18-year high mortgage stress, 10% house price decline forecast, potential fourth RBA hike create downside risk for REITs and banks

defensive_moves.recommendation: Avoid Qantas and corporate travel names
defensive_moves.rationale: Strike vote, cost-cutting, and CTX plunge signal near-term operational and demand headwinds

defensive_moves.recommendation: Maintain defensive dividend and healthcare allocation
defensive_moves.rationale: Stagflation risk and productivity decline favour resilient cash-flow businesses

market_outlook.short_term: ASX likely range-bound to modestly lower. RBA rate-hike uncertainty, mortgage stress, and geopolitical risk (Persian Gulf, China) cap upside. Gold and energy provide pockets of strength. QAN.AX and CTX.AX drag on transport. Trust tax debate adds policy noise.
market_outlook.long_term: Productivity 'bad to worse' and narrow recession avoidance suggest structural headwinds. Energy transition cost overruns and housing correction risk weigh on GDP. However, critical minerals, gold, and AI infrastructure offer secular growth pockets. RBA likely to pause or slow hikes if housing stress deepens.
